# R packages

All subsequent analyses were performed in `R` using the following packages.

-   R 4.5.2
-   tidyverse 2.0.0
-   colorspace 2.1-2
-   vegan 2.7-3
-   philentropy 0.10.0
-   phyloseq 1.54.2
-   ggpubr 0.6.3
-   ggbeeswarm 0.7.3
-   ANCOMBC 2.12.0
-   ALDEx2 1.42.0
-   microbiome 1.32.0

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(colorspace)
library(vegan)
library(philentropy)
library(phyloseq)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(ANCOMBC)
library(ALDEx2)
```

# Data import

## Formatting of abundance table

The species-level abundance table (`wf-16s-counts-species.csv`) was imported and formatted for downstream analysis.

```{r}
# Import abundance table
# Remove rows classified as "Unknown"
counts_raw <- read.csv(
  "wf-16s-counts-species.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
) %>%
  dplyr::filter(species != "Unknown")

sample_cols <- names(counts_raw)[
  2:(which(names(counts_raw) == "total") - 1)
]

# Taxonomic ranks available in the wf-16s output
tax_levels <- c(
  "species",
  "genus",
  "family",
  "order",
  "class",
  "phylum"
)
```

## Abundance filtering

To minimize noise and eliminate potentially spurious reads, taxa that did not reach a relative abundance threshold (e.g., `0.25%`) in any single sample were removed. The abundance-filtered count table was defined as `counts_filt`.

::: user-setting
**User-defined parameter**

Modify the abundance filter threshold in `make_tax_table()`:

[abundance_threshold = 0.0025]{.user-param}
:::

```{r}
# Function to generate taxonomic count tables
make_tax_table <- function(
    counts_raw,
    sample_cols,
    tax_level,
    abundance_threshold = 0.0025
) {

  cat("Processing:", tax_level, "\n")

  # Collapse taxa to selected rank
  counts_tax <- counts_raw %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[tax_level]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[tax_level]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      across(all_of(sample_cols), sum),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    as.data.frame()

  rownames(counts_tax) <- counts_tax[[tax_level]]
  counts_tax[[tax_level]] <- NULL

  # Calculate relative abundance
  rel <- sweep(counts_tax, 2, colSums(counts_tax), "/")

  # Abundance filter (retain taxa reaching ≥0.25% in at least one sample)
  counts_filt <- counts_tax[
    rowSums(
      rel >= abundance_threshold,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) > 0,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  return(
    list(
      counts_tax = counts_tax,
      counts_filt = counts_filt
    )
  )

}
```

## Generation of taxonomic count tables

Taxonomic count tables were generated for each rank (species, genus, family, order, class, and phylum).

```{r}
# Create taxonomic count tables for all ranks
results <- lapply(
  tax_levels,
  function(x)
    make_tax_table(
      counts_raw = counts_raw,
      sample_cols = sample_cols,
      tax_level = x
    )
)

names(results) <- tax_levels
```

## Metadata table

A sample metadata table (`metadata.csv`) was prepared to define group assignments for downstream analyses. The table included sample identifiers and corresponding group information.

Example format:

::: {style="max-width: 200px;"}
| sample | group   |
|--------|---------|
| N01    | non-LCS |
| N02    | non-LCS |
| ...    | non-LCS |
| W01    | LCS     |
| W02    | LCS     |
| ...    | LCS     |
:::

The metadata file was loaded into the `metadata` object for subsequent analyses.

::: user-setting
**User-defined parameter**

Enter the names of the reference and target groups as they appear in the metadata file:

group_order \<- c("\<reference\>", "\<target\>")

[group_order \<- c("non-LCS", "LCS")]{.user-param}
:::

```{r}
# Import sample metadata
metadata <- read.csv("metadata.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# Define reference and target groups (e.g., non-LCS as reference)
group_order <- c("non-LCS", "LCS")

metadata$group <- factor(
  metadata$group,
  levels = group_order
)

ref_group <- group_order[1]
target_group <- group_order[2]

# Define colors for each group
cols_map <- setNames(
  c("#1f78b4", "#fb6a4a"),
  group_order
)
```

# Community composition

Taxonomic composition was assessed using abundance-filtered count tables (`counts_filt`). For each taxonomic rank (species to phylum), relative abundances were calculated to generate composition tables. Taxa reaching relative abundance threshold (e.g., `≥10%`) in at least one sample were classified as major taxa, while all remaining taxa were combined into an "Others" category. Taxonomic composition was visualized using stacked bar plots.

::: user-setting
**User-defined parameter**

Modify the relative abundance threshold (%) used to define major taxa in `make_composition_plot()`:

[major_threshold = 10]{.user-param}
:::

## Function definitions

```{r}
# Function to generate composition tables and plots
make_composition_plot <- function(
    counts,
    tax_level,
    output_suffix = "",
    major_threshold = 10
) {

  # Convert to relative abundance (%)
  relative <- t(counts)

  relative <- relative /
    rowSums(relative) * 100

  relative <- as.data.frame(relative)

  # Define major taxa
  major_taxa <- colnames(relative)[
    apply(relative, 2, max) >= major_threshold
  ]

  minor_taxa <- setdiff(
    colnames(relative),
    major_taxa
  )

  composition <- relative[
    ,
    major_taxa,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  if (length(minor_taxa) > 0) {

    composition$Others <- rowSums(
      relative[
        ,
        minor_taxa,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )
  }

  # Sort taxa by mean abundance
  if (length(major_taxa) > 0) {

    avg_abundance <- colMeans(
      composition[
        ,
        major_taxa,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )

    sorted <- names(
      sort(
        avg_abundance,
        decreasing = TRUE
      )
    )

    if ("Others" %in% colnames(composition)) {

      composition <- composition[
        ,
        c(sorted, "Others"),
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    } else {
      
      composition <- composition[
        ,
        sorted,
        drop = FALSE
      ]        
    }
  }  

  # Export tables
  write.csv(
    relative,
    paste0(
      "comp_all_",
      output_suffix,
      tax_level,
      ".csv"
    )
  )

  write.csv(
    composition,
    paste0(
      "comp_major_",
      output_suffix,
      tax_level,
      ".csv"
    )
  )

  # Prepare plotting data
  composition$Sample <- rownames(composition)

  comp_long <- composition %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = -Sample,
      names_to = "Taxon",
      values_to = "Abundance"
    )

  taxa_order <- setdiff(
    colnames(composition),
    "Sample"
  )

  comp_long$Taxon <- factor(
    comp_long$Taxon,
    levels = taxa_order
  )

  # Generate color palette
  num_major_taxa <- sum(
    taxa_order != "Others"
  )
  
  if (num_major_taxa > 0) {
    
    custom_colors <- colorspace::qualitative_hcl(
      n = max(num_major_taxa, 1),
      palette = "Dynamic"
    )

    names(custom_colors) <-
      taxa_order[taxa_order != "Others"]
    
  } else {
    
    custom_colors <- c()
  }
 
  if ("Others" %in% taxa_order) {
    
    full_colors <- c(
      custom_colors,
      Others = "#d0d0d0"
    )
    
  } else {
    
    full_colors <- custom_colors
  
  }
  
  # Taxon label font style
  taxon_face <- if (
    tax_level %in% c("species", "genus")
  ) {
    "italic"
  } else {
    "plain"
  }

  # Create stacked bar plot
  p_bar <- ggplot(
    comp_long,
    aes(
      x = Sample,
      y = Abundance,
      fill = Taxon
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.8,
      position = position_stack(
        reverse = TRUE
      )
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = full_colors
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(0, 100)
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Relative abundance (%)",
      fill = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 1,
        size = 9
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.key.size = unit(0.25, "cm"),
      legend.spacing.y = unit(0.05, "cm"),
      legend.text = element_text(
        size = 8,
        face = taxon_face
      ),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        color = "#d9d9d9"
      ),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  # Export plot
  ggsave(
    paste0(
      "comp_plot_",
      output_suffix,
      tax_level,
      ".pdf"
    ),
    plot = p_bar,
    width = 9.5,
    height = 5
  )

  invisible(NULL)

}
```

## Composition tables and plots

```{r}
# Generate composition tables and stacked bar plots for all taxonomic ranks
lapply(
  tax_levels,
  function(x) {
    
    make_composition_plot(
      counts = results[[x]]$counts_filt,
      tax_level = x,
      output_suffix = "full_"
    )
    
  }  
)
```

For each taxonomic rank (species, genus, family, order, class, and phylum):

-   `comp_major_full_<rank>.csv`

# Taxonomic rank selection

The taxonomic rank used for rarefaction, diversity analyses, and differential abundance testing was specified as follows. The example below is shown for `genus-level` analysis.

::: user-setting
**User-defined parameter**

Select the taxonomic rank for downstream analyses:

[tax_level \<- "genus"]{.user-param}

Available options: `"phylum"`, `"class"`, `"order"`, `"family"`, `"genus"`, `"species"`.
:::

```{r}
# Select count table for downstream analyses
tax_level <- "genus"

counts_filt <- results[[tax_level]]$counts_filt

# Taxon label font style
taxon_face <- if (
  tax_level %in% c("species", "genus")
) {
  "italic"
} else {
  "plain"
}
```

# Rarefaction analysis

Rarefaction curves were generated using the filtered dataset (`counts_filt`) at the selected taxonomic rank to assess sequencing depth across samples.

## Rarefaction curves

```{r}
# Match sample order
metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts_filt), , drop = FALSE]

# Assign colors to samples based on group
cols <- cols_map[as.character(metadata$group)]

# Plot and export rarefaction curves using all reads
pdf(
  paste0(
    "rarecurve_full_",
    tax_level,
    ".pdf"
  ),   
  width = 6,
  height = 5,
  pointsize = 10
)

par(
  cex.lab = 1.0,
  cex.axis = 0.9
)

rarecurve(
  t(counts_filt),
  step = 100,
  col = adjustcolor(cols, alpha.f = 0.6),
  lwd = 2,
  label = FALSE,
  xlab = "Number of reads",
  ylab = "Observed taxa"
)

legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = group_order,
  col = cols_map[group_order],
  lty = 1,
  lwd = 2,
  bty = "n",
  cex = 1.0
)

dev.off()
```

#### Outputs {.unnumbered .unlisted}

-   `rarecurve_full_<rank>.pdf`

## Sequencing depth estimation

To assess sequencing depth sufficiency, taxonomic coverage was estimated using rarefaction curves across a range of sequencing depths (e.g., 1,000–20,000 reads). Coverage represented the proportion of observed taxa at each depth relative to the maximum richness per sample. The mean taxonomic coverage was calculated to determine the optimal rarefaction depth for downstream analyses.

::: user-setting
**User-defined parameter**

Specify the sequencing depth range and interval for taxonomic coverage estimation:

step = \<interval\>

depths \<- seq(\<minimum_depth\>, \<maximum_depth\>, by = \<interval\>)

[step = 100]{.user-param}

[depths \<- seq(1000, 20000, by = 1000)]{.user-param}

For consistency, depth interval (`by`) should match `step` or be an integer multiple of `step`.
:::

```{r}
# Generate rarefaction curves
# `step`: interval at which rarefaction values are calculated.
rare_data <- rarecurve(
  t(counts_filt),
  step = 100,
  sample = NULL,
  label = FALSE,
  tidy = TRUE
)

# Obtain filtered read counts for each sample
sample_depths <- rare_data %>%
  group_by(Site) %>%
  summarise(
    reads = max(Sample),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate taxonomic coverage at each depth
depths <- seq(1000, 20000, by = 1000)

coverage <- lapply(depths, function(target_depth) {
  rare_data %>%
    group_by(Site) %>%
    summarise(
      max_taxa = max(Species),
      max_reads = max(Sample),
      taxa_at_depth = if (
        target_depth <= max_reads &&
        any(Sample <= target_depth)
      ) {
        max(Species[Sample <= target_depth], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      coverage = if (!is.na(max_taxa) && max_taxa > 0) {
        round(taxa_at_depth / max_taxa * 100, 2)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(depth = target_depth)

}) %>%
  bind_rows()

# Create coverage table
coverage_res <- coverage %>%
  dplyr::select(Site, depth, coverage) %>%
  mutate(depth = paste0("Depth_", depth)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = depth,
    values_from = coverage
  ) %>%
  left_join(sample_depths, by = "Site") %>%
  relocate(reads, .after = Site)

# Summarize taxonomic coverage across samples at each sequencing depth
coverage_summary <- coverage %>%
  group_by(depth) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_coverage = mean(coverage, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_coverage = sd(coverage, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_samples = sum(!is.na(coverage)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Export results
write.csv(
  coverage_res,
  paste0("cov_res_", tax_level, ".csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  coverage_summary,
  paste0("cov_summ_", tax_level, ".csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

#### Outputs {.unnumbered .unlisted}

-   `cov_res_<rank>.csv`
-   `cov_summ_<rank>.csv`

# Preparation of analysis datasets

Samples with sequencing depths below the selected rarefaction threshold were excluded from the abundance-filtered count table. The resulting dataset was defined as `counts_depth`. For diversity analyses, `counts_depth` was rarefied to the selected sequencing depth, generating `counts_rare`. Rarefaction curves up to the defined read depth were constructed to highlight the initial slope. Additionally, composition tables and stacked bar plots at the selected sequencing depth and taxonomic rank were generated using the `counts_rare` dataset.

::: user-setting
**User-defined parameter**

Specify the rarefaction threshold (reads per sample) used to generate the rarefied dataset:

[rarefaction_depth \<- 4900]{.user-param}
:::

```{r}
# Determine rarefaction depth
rarefaction_depth <- 4900

# Exclude samples below the selected rarefaction depth
counts_depth <- counts_filt[, colSums(counts_filt) >= rarefaction_depth, drop = FALSE]

# Rarefy counts to a fixed depth
set.seed(123)
counts_rare <- t(
  rrarefy(
    t(counts_depth),
    sample = rarefaction_depth
  )
)

# Match sample order
metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts_rare), , drop = FALSE]
cols <- cols_map[as.character(metadata$group)]

# Generate truncated rarefaction curves up to the defined read depth.
pdf(
  paste0(
    "rarecurve_trunc_",
    tax_level,
    ".pdf"
  ),  
  width = 6,
  height = 5,
  pointsize = 10
)

par(
  cex.lab = 1.0,
  cex.axis = 0.9
)

rarecurve(
  t(counts_depth),
  step = 50,
  xlim = c(0, rarefaction_depth),
  col = adjustcolor(cols, alpha.f = 0.6),
  lwd = 2,
  label = FALSE,
  xlab = "Number of reads",
  ylab = "Observed taxa"
)

legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = group_order,
  col = cols_map[group_order],
  lty = 1,
  lwd = 2,
  bty = "n",
  cex = 1.0
)

dev.off()

# Generate composition tables and stacked bar plots using rarefied counts.
make_composition_plot(
  counts = counts_rare,
  tax_level = tax_level,
  output_suffix = "rare_"
)
```

#### Outputs {.unnumbered .unlisted}

-   `rarecurve_trunc_<rank>.pdf`
-   `comp_all_rare_<rank>.csv`
-   `comp_major_rare_<rank>.csv`
-   `comp_plot_rare_<rank>.pdf`

# Alpha diversity

## Estimation of alpha diversity indices

Alpha diversity metrics, including the observed `richness` and `Shannon index`, were calculated based on the `counts_rare` dataset.

```{r}
# Match sample order
metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts_rare), , drop = FALSE]

# Calculate richness (number of observed taxa)
richness <- vegan::specnumber(t(counts_rare))

# Calculate Shannon diversity index
shannon <- vegan::diversity(t(counts_rare), index = "shannon")

# Create alpha diversity table
df_alpha <- data.frame(
  Richness = richness,
  Shannon  = shannon
)

plot_data <- cbind(metadata, df_alpha)

plot_data$group <- factor(
  plot_data$group,
  levels = group_order
)

# --- Console Output ---
cat("\n==============================\n")
cat(" Summary statistics by group\n")
cat("==============================\n")

cat("\n=== Richness ===\n")
by(plot_data$Richness, plot_data$group, summary)

cat("\n=== Shannon ===\n")
by(plot_data$Shannon, plot_data$group, summary)

cat("\n==============================\n")
cat(" Wilcoxon rank-sum tests\n")
cat("==============================\n")

cat("\n=== Richness ===\n")
wilcox_richness <- wilcox.test(Richness ~ group, data = plot_data)
print(wilcox_richness)

cat("\n=== Shannon ===\n")
wilcox_shannon <- wilcox.test(Shannon ~ group, data = plot_data)
print(wilcox_shannon)

# Export results
write.csv(
  plot_data,
  file = paste0("alpha_", tax_level, ".csv")
)  
```

#### Outputs {.unnumbered .unlisted}

-   `alpha_<rank>.csv`

```{r}
# Save plots as PDF
```

# Beta diversity

Beta diversity was assessed using the `counts_rare` dataset with three measures of community dissimilarity: `Bray–Curtis` dissimilarity, `Jaccard` distance, and `Jensen–Shannon` distance (JSD). Differences in community composition between groups were evaluated using permutational multivariate analysis of variance (`PERMANOVA`), and patterns of community dissimilarity were visualized using principal coordinates analysis (`PCoA`). Group assignments were based on the `metadata`. For JSD, the square root of Jensen–Shannon divergence was used to obtain a distance measure for subsequent analyses.

## Distance matrix calculation and statistical testing

```{r}
# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity
bray_curtis <- vegdist(
  t(counts_rare),
  method = "bray"
)

# Jaccard dissimilarity (binary)
jaccard <- vegdist(
  t(counts_rare),
  method = "jaccard",
  binary = TRUE
)

# Jensen-Shannon divergence
# Convert counts to relative abundance
rel_abund <- t(counts_rare)

rel_abund <- sweep(
  rel_abund,
  1,
  rowSums(rel_abund),
  "/"
)

rownames(rel_abund) <- colnames(counts_rare)

# Calculate Jensen-Shannon divergence
jsd <- philentropy::distance(
  rel_abund,
  method = "jensen-shannon"
)

# Restore sample names
rownames(jsd) <- colnames(counts_rare)
colnames(jsd) <- colnames(counts_rare)

# Convert divergence to Jensen-Shannon distance
js_distance <- as.dist(sqrt(jsd))

# Match sample order
metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts_rare), , drop = FALSE]

metadata$group <- factor(
  metadata$group,
  levels = group_order
)

# PERMANOVA (Bray-Curtis)
set.seed(123)
permanova_bray <- adonis2(
  bray_curtis ~ group,
  data = metadata
)

# PERMANOVA (Jaccard)
set.seed(123)
permanova_jaccard <- adonis2(
  jaccard ~ group,
  data = metadata
)

# PERMANOVA (Jensen-Shannon)
set.seed(123)
permanova_jsd <- adonis2(
  js_distance ~ group,
  data = metadata
)

# --- Console Output ---

cat("\n--- PERMANOVA (Bray-Curtis) ---\n")
cat("R-squared:", round(permanova_bray$R2[1], 3), "\n")
cat("P-value:", permanova_bray$`Pr(>F)`[1], "\n")

cat("\n--- PERMANOVA (Jaccard) ---\n")
cat("R-squared:", round(permanova_jaccard$R2[1], 3), "\n")
cat("P-value:", permanova_jaccard$`Pr(>F)`[1], "\n")

cat("\n--- PERMANOVA (Jensen-Shannon) ---\n")
cat("R-squared:", round(permanova_jsd$R2[1], 3), "\n")
cat("P-value:", permanova_jsd$`Pr(>F)`[1], "\n")
```

## Visualization by PCoA

```{r}
# Define a common function for PCoA
run_pcoa <- function(
  distance_matrix,
  permanova_result,
  method_name,
  metadata,
  cols_map,
  group_order,
  tax_level
) {

  # PCoA
  pcoa_result <- cmdscale(
    distance_matrix,
    k = 2,
    eig = TRUE
  )

  # Construct the plotting dataset
  pcoa_points <- as.data.frame(pcoa_result$points)

  colnames(pcoa_points) <- c(
    "PCoA1",
    "PCoA2"
  )

  pcoa_points$group <- metadata$group

  # Calculate variance explained by each axis
  eig_values <- pcoa_result$eig

  positive_eig <- eig_values[
    eig_values > 0
  ]

  variance_explained <- (
    positive_eig /
    sum(positive_eig)
  )

  var1 <- round(
    variance_explained[1] * 100,
    1
  )

  var2 <- round(
    variance_explained[2] * 100,
    1
  )

  # Format PERMANOVA results
  permanova_label <- paste0(
    "PERMANOVA\n",
    "R² = ", round(permanova_result$R2[1], 3),
    "\n",
    "P = ", signif(permanova_result$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3)
  )

  # Visualize PCoA results
  p_pcoa <- ggplot(
    pcoa_points,
    aes(
      x = PCoA1,
      y = PCoA2,
      color = group,
      fill = group
    )
  ) +
    stat_ellipse(
      geom = "polygon",
      type = "t",
      alpha = 0.2,
      color = NA
    ) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = Inf,
      y = Inf,
      label = permanova_label,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 3.5
    ) +
    coord_fixed() +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = cols_map,
      breaks = group_order
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = cols_map,
      breaks = group_order
    ) +
    labs(
      x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var1, "%)"),
      y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var2, "%)"),
      color = NULL,
      fill = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 10)
    )

  # Save plot to file
  ggsave(
    paste0("pcoa_", method_name, "_", tax_level, ".pdf"),
    plot = p_pcoa,
    width = 6,
    height = 5
  )

  # Return PCoA results and plot
  return(list(
    pcoa = pcoa_result,
    points = pcoa_points,
    plot = p_pcoa
  ))
}

# PCoA (Bray-Curtis)
result_bray <- run_pcoa(
  distance_matrix = bray_curtis,
  permanova_result = permanova_bray,
  method_name = "bray",
  metadata = metadata,
  cols_map = cols_map,
  group_order = group_order,
  tax_level = tax_level
)

# PCoA (Jaccard)
result_jaccard <- run_pcoa(
  distance_matrix = jaccard,
  permanova_result = permanova_jaccard,
  method_name = "jaccard",
  metadata = metadata,
  cols_map = cols_map,
  group_order = group_order,
  tax_level = tax_level
)

# PCoA (Jensen-Shannon)
result_jsd <- run_pcoa(
  distance_matrix = js_distance,
  permanova_result = permanova_jsd,
  method_name = "jsd",
  metadata = metadata,
  cols_map = cols_map,
  group_order = group_order,
  tax_level = tax_level
)
```

-   `pcoa_jaccard_<rank>.pdf`
-   `pcoa_jsd_<rank>.pdf`

# Differential abundance

To identify bacterial taxa with significantly different abundances between groups, differential abundance analysis (`DAA`) was performed.

## Prevalence filtering

Prevalence filtering was applied to the non-rarefied dataset (`counts_depth`) to exclude taxa detected in fewer than `two` samples, thereby reducing noise from sparsely observed taxa and improving statistical robustness. The resulting filtered data (`counts_prv`) were used for the analysis, applying group information from the `metadata` object.

::: user-setting
**User-defined parameter**

Specify the prevalence threshold (minimum number of samples in which a taxon must be detected):

[counts_prv \<- counts_depth\[rowSums(counts_depth \> 0) \>= 2, \]]{.user-param}
:::

```{r}
# Prevalence filtering (retain taxa detected in ≥2 samples)
counts_prv <- counts_depth[rowSums(counts_depth > 0) >= 2, ]

# Match sample order
metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts_prv), , drop = FALSE]
metadata$group <- factor(
  metadata$group,
  levels = group_order
  )
```

## Analysis of Compositions of Microbiomes with Bias Correction 2 (ANCOM-BC2)

### Statistical analysis

Differentially abundant taxa were identified using `ANCOM-BC2` (q \< 0.05). Taxa passing the sensitivity analysis were classified as robust findings, while those detected without the sensitivity score filter were considered exploratory.

```{r}
# Construct phyloseq object
tax_matrix <- data.frame(Taxa = rownames(counts_prv))
rownames(tax_matrix) <- rownames(counts_prv)

ps <- phyloseq(
  otu_table(counts_prv, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
  sample_data(metadata),
  tax_table(as.matrix(tax_matrix))
)

# Run ANCOM-BC2
out <- ancombc2(
  data = ps,
  fix_formula = "group",
  tax_level = NULL,
  p_adj_method = "fdr",
  prv_cut = 0,
  group = "group",
  struc_zero = TRUE,
  neg_lb = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05
)

# Extract results
res_ancom <- out$res

# Column indicating exploratory significance
diff_group_col <- paste0("diff_group", target_group)

# Column indicating robust significance
diff_robust_col <- paste0("diff_robust_group", target_group)

# Add significance label
res_ancom$significance <- ifelse(
  res_ancom[[diff_group_col]], "*", "ns")

res_ancom$significance_robust <- ifelse(
  res_ancom[[diff_robust_col]], "*", "ns")

# Export full results table
write.csv(
  res_ancom,
  paste0("ancom_", tax_level, ".csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

#### Outputs {.unnumbered .unlisted}

-   `ancom_<rank>.csv`

### Visualization of ANCOM-BC2 results

Log fold changes estimated by ANCOM-BC2 were visualized as bar plots. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals.

```{r}
# Prepare ANCOM-BC2 results
lfc_col <- paste0("lfc_group", target_group)
se_col <- paste0("se_group", target_group)

df_ancom <- res_ancom %>%
  arrange(.data[[lfc_col]]) %>%
  mutate(
    group_direction = ifelse(
      .data[[lfc_col]] > 0,
      target_group,
      ref_group
    ),

    ci_lower = .data[[lfc_col]] -
      1.96 * .data[[se_col]],

    ci_upper = .data[[lfc_col]] +
      1.96 * .data[[se_col]]
  )

df_ancom$group_direction <- factor(
  df_ancom$group_direction,
  levels = c(target_group, ref_group)
)
```

#### Top taxa by absolute log fold change {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```{r}

  ) %>%

  df_ancom_top$taxon,

# Generate bar plot of log fold change with confidence intervals

) +

  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,

  ) +

  ) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("Log fold change (", target_group, " vs ", ref_group, ")"),
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#eeeeee"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = taxon_face, size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )

# Save plot to file
ggsave(
  paste0("ancom_top_", tax_level, ".pdf"),
  plot = p_ancom_top,
  width = 6,
  height = 5
)
```

## ANOVA-Like Differential Expression (ALDEx2)

### Statistical analysis

Differential abundance analysis was performed using `ALDEx2`. Taxa with a Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted Wilcoxon test p-value (wi.eBH) \< 0.05 were considered significantly different between groups.

```{r}
# Define group variable
conds <- as.character(metadata$group)

conds <- ifelse(
  conds == ref_group,
  paste0("1_", ref_group),
  paste0("2_", target_group)
)

# CLR transformation with Monte Carlo sampling
set.seed(123)
x <- aldex.clr(
  counts_prv,
  conds,
  mc.samples = 256,
  denom = "all",
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Statistical testing
aldex_test <- aldex.ttest(x)

# Effect size estimation
aldex_effect <- aldex.effect(x)

# Combine results
res_aldex <- data.frame(aldex_test, aldex_effect)

# Add significance label
res_aldex$significance <- ifelse(
  res_aldex$wi.eBH < 0.05, "*", "ns")

# Export results
write.csv(
  res_aldex,
  paste0("aldex_", tax_level, ".csv"),
  row.names = TRUE
)
```

#### Outputs {.unnumbered .unlisted}

-   `aldex_<rank>.csv`

### Visualization of ALDEx2 results

Effect sizes estimated by ALDEx2 were visualized as bar plots.

```{r}
# Prepare ALDEx2 results
df_aldex <- res_aldex %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("taxon") %>%
  arrange(effect) %>%
  mutate(
    group_direction = ifelse(effect > 0, target_group, ref_group)
  )

df_aldex$group_direction <- factor(
  df_aldex$group_direction,
  levels = c(target_group, ref_group)
)
```
